title: ILNP: Add Dissector (RFC 6740 - RFC 6748)
description:
Implemented a dissector for the ILNP protocol in files dissectors/packet-ilnp.c and dissectors/packet-ilnp.h.
The Identifier-Locator Network Protocol (ILNP) is a network-layer protocol designed to enhance the scalability, flexibility, and mobility of the Internet. It builds upon the foundation of IPv6, addressing some of the inherent limitations of traditional IP addressing, particularly in the
areas of mobility, multihoming, and network management. Unlike IPv6, which uses a single, atomic address to identify the topological location of a device globally, ILNP separates the network location and the device’s identity.
This meant I also had to modify other dissectors like the IPv6, TCP and UDP dissectors to work with ILNP.

Hello. Thank you for your help with this. This is my first large scale project so I do not know how to squash commits as I keep making new ones. 

I am using the ILNP dataset collected during the IETF118 Hackathon which can be found here https://research-portal.st-andrews.ac.uk/en/datasets/ilnp-identifier-locator-network-protocol-freebsd-140-ietf118pragu. I can also share just the capture pcap files. How should I share these?
Since this was my dissertation project I also have the dissertation report which explains what ILNP is, what I implemented and why, how to expand on it and testing tables. I can also share this if it will be helpful.

Finally, I also am looking for some guidance on calling the ILNP dissector. There is no actual ILNP indicator. The only way to determine an ILNP packet is to look for the ILNP Nonce destination options header during the IPv6 dissector. My solution is to check for this before the IPv6 dissector runs and call the ILNP dissector using a copy of the buffer (as I would like for both dissectors to run using the same buffer data). But this is inefficient as the check runs for every single IPv6 packet. I do not know how to call the ILNP dissector as the nonce header is found during regular IPv6 dissection with the full network layer packet buffer; from my understanding, the buffer pointer is moved forward as the packet is dissected and previous bytes cannot be accessed. 
Further, since there are two source addresses (NID and L64) and two destination addresses in an ILNP packet, a single pinfo->src/pinfo->net address field is not enough. 

I greatly appreciate any advice.

I've looked at the code and briefly looked at the RFC.  It's going to be a struggle with semantics (and the definition of "protocol" from a Wireshark perspective). To me the logic can be summarized as:

**If there is a ILNP Nonce destination option in an IPv6 packet, treat the bytes used for source/destination address for IPv6 differently** (let's call them "stringified")

ILNP has no bearing on the IPv6 payload, so it shouldn't even try.  It really just wants to present a different way to filter on (IPv6) addresses. So, from that perspective I'm not sure it needs its own "protocol file" (and all logic should remain in packet-ipv6.c).

What I was most curious of was the "address layering" and how this patch handled it.  Looking at the code, it seems to want to keep the "network layer" addressing untouched and work with the "top layer" source/destination address replacing the IPv6 addressing with the "stringified" version.  The packet data (that feeds into the address structure) isn't any different, it's just the interpretation of the bytes.  But is the ILNP protocol "replacing" IPv6 from a network layer perspective so it should overwrite the "network layer" address with its stringified version?

From a high level, ILNP seems to be "breaking up" the IPv6 address to optimizing routing.  For sake of argument let's just break it up into "left" (first 8 bytes) and "right" (last 8 bytes).  Is one of the goals to be able to create a filter that will consider "all packets with a matching "left" value its own stream"?  Maybe something similar with a "right" stream?  I think that can be accomplished today with IPv6 fields, but the filter probably looks "overly complex".

Overall, it seems like what ILNP functionality is after is more flexibility with "address fields" than dissecting bytes.  So I think that can be accomplished in the IPv6 dissector with some additional "generated" fields (for all of the addresses) if the Nonce field is present (so maybe the generated fields should be in the Nonce subtree?)

Hope this helps.  It's a cool idea, but I think the initial approach needs some work.

Thank you for the advice, I will look into implementing it that way. 

ILNP is meant to be a separate protocol to IPv6 but built in a way that current infrastructure does not need to be updated to use (by using the same packet structure as IPv6). Since ILNP is still a research topic it is useful to have both the IPv6 and ILNP dissections. 

For some context, ILNP does change how flow/conversation tracking and the TCP/UDP checksums are handled and processed since the first 8 bytes of the address can change during a flow (Using ICMPv6 Locator Update messages). So ILNP specific conversation handling is required and the TCP/UDP dissectors should use only the last 8 bytes (the node identifier) in all their processing, otherwise the TCP conversation completeness and TCP+UDP checksums are incorrectly calculated.
I have a few ideas that are much faster to code than explain, so I'll create a second MR that we can use as a talking point (I don't want to overwrite your current work).
